hyps.why: Dropping a parameterless skip on edge 0 is harmless or even helpful (+41 in the all-skip parent, +2 to +3 in another), whereas dropping a conv hurts.
Removing an avg-pool loses no learnable capacity and was non-negative in both avg-pool parents on every dataset.
Removing a 3x3 conv from the input edge cuts representational capacity and was negative in all four such parents on every dataset.
Removing a learnable 1x1 conv on edge 0 hurt in both parents tested, on all three datasets.
Replacing a parameter-free avg-pool shortcut with nothing costs little (and helped in both avg-pool parents), unlike removing a conv.
Deleting the direct 3x3 conv edge from input to output removes a major learnable path, causing large drops especially on ImageNet16-120.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with avg-pool discards learnable capacity, hurting more than replacing a 1x1 conv.
Swapping a parameterless avg-pool for a learnable 1x1 conv gains capacity (+30 in the all-avg-pool parent, +2 in another), unlike replacing an existing 3x3 conv.
Downgrading a 3x3 conv to 1x1 reduces receptive field and capacity, giving small negative changes.
Replacing a 3x3 conv on the intermediate edge with a parameterless skip loses capacity and was negative in both parents tested.
